app.name: Gmail (Gmail API through your own Google Cloud OAuth client)

verdict.summary: Setting up your own client for testing takes minutes, but any public use of Gmail scopes is gated by Google verification, and the full-mailbox scope that Composio's defaults include adds an annual CASA security assessment. Most of the difficulty is the Gmail restricted scope, not the setup itself.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1-2 hours for Gate 1 setup and test; several days of work to assemble the Gate 3 submission package (brand, scope justifications, demo video), plus the assessment.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Under an hour for your own Google account (estimate; the developer console is login-gated and was not walked through).
verdict.approval_wait: None for your own account. For restricted-scope verification, about six weeks is community-reported and unverified; CASA assessment timing was not found.

gates.name: Testing status, your own account
gates.unlocks: You can connect your own Google account to an OAuth client you created in your own Google Cloud project.
limits: External apps in Testing are for test users only; the consent screen will not serve general users (see Gate 2 limits).
Non-sensitive-only apps are not required to pass full verification (f12).
Google only grants newly added scopes at consent time, so a user who consented earlier must re-consent (community, f29).

gates.name: Testing status with test users (or Internal, Workspace only)
gates.unlocks: Up to 100 invited test users can authorize the app. If your account belongs to a Google Workspace organization, the Internal user type is available and skips verification.
limits: Hard cap of 100 test users for External apps in Testing (community-reported, f22; not confirmed for Gmail scopes on an official page).
Refresh tokens for External Testing apps expire after 7 days (community, f23). Internal apps are exempt (community, f23).

Refresh tokens can also stop working after six months unused, on user revocation, after a password change when Gmail scopes are included, or at the per-user, per-client refresh token limit (community, f24).
Internal user type is only available for apps created under a Google Workspace Organization (f7).
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes after Gate 1, once test users are added.

gates.name: Production, verified (anyone can sign in)
gates.unlocks: Any Google user can grant access to the app.
limits: Restricted scopes such as https://mail.google.com/ require a verification submission with a demo video, plus an annual security assessment by a Google-approved assessor (f10, f13, f15).
Assurance level is AL1 or AL2; AL2 stays in later years (f16).
Every app must be revalidated every year (f21).
CASA lab fee of about $540 to $1,000 is community-reported and unconfirmed (f17).
A community guide says users cannot grant access to a production app past the test-user cap until verification passes (community, f25).
gates.time_to_reach: Community-reported around six weeks for restricted-scope verification (unverified). CASA assessment timing not found.

steps.title: Decide: Composio managed auth or your own OAuth client
steps.detail: Composio's managed OAUTH2 config for Gmail is the fast path for prototyping, and its default scopes include the full-mailbox scope. For any external users you will need your own Google OAuth client, because Composio's managed client's verification status for these scopes is unknown. Choose your scope set before you create the consent screen, since scopes drive review.
gotchas: Default Composio scopes include https://mail.google.com/, which Google classes as restricted.

steps.title: Create or select a Google Cloud project
steps.detail: Sign in to the Google Cloud console with the Google account that will own the app. Create a new project or select an existing one; the OAuth app must be tied to a Google Cloud project before scopes can be added.
gotchas: The console is behind Google sign-in; unauthenticated visits redirect to a login page.

steps.title: Set the user type on the OAuth consent screen
steps.detail: Open the OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform) and choose a user type. Choose Internal only if the project belongs to a Google Workspace organization; that option skips verification. Otherwise choose External, which starts in Testing status.
gotchas: Internal is only offered to Google Workspace organization apps (f7).
Exact menu labels were not verified in this session; check the official OAuth overview.

steps.title: Fill in app branding and the privacy policy link
steps.detail: Enter the app name, support email and logo on the consent screen. Brand verification needs a homepage on a domain you own that describes the app (not a login page), and the privacy policy must be linked from that homepage and from the consent screen. Google's Gmail data rules also restrict transfers and human access to Gmail data.

values.label: Homepage
values.value: A page on a domain you own that describes the app

values.label: Privacy policy
values.value: Linked from homepage and consent screen

gotchas: Brand verification is needed even when only non-sensitive scopes are used, to show name and logo (f12).

steps.title: Add the scopes, narrowest first
steps.detail: Add only the scopes your features need. Google sorts each scope into non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted when you add it; check the classification list before you go further. Start with the sign-in scopes and a narrow Gmail scope rather than the full mailbox scope if you can.
gotchas: Google expects only the narrowest scopes your app needs, with a written justification (f11).
Composio's default scope list is long (contacts, birthday, addresses, phone numbers); the classification of those is not in the findings, so check the console before you rely on them.

steps.title: Add your test users
steps.detail: In the audience section of the consent screen, add the Google accounts that should be able to sign in while the app is in Testing. You can add up to 100 for External apps.
gotchas: Refresh tokens for test users expire after 7 days (community-reported). Plan to re-authorize.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client and set the redirect URI
steps.detail: On the Credentials page, create an OAuth client ID of the Web application type. Under authorized redirect URIs, paste the callback URL from your Composio auth config. The exact labels in the console were not verified in this session, so follow the screen as it appears.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Google's authorize endpoint rejects unknown client IDs with invalid_client, so the client must exist before Composio can use it (probed).
Paste the exact callback URL, including the protocol and path.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the client ID and client secret from the new OAuth client. Create a custom auth config for the gmail toolkit in Composio and paste both values. Keep the secret out of source control.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: An agent with access to the Composio auth config can start a connection flow with your own Google account and confirm the token exchange succeeds. Check that the granted scopes match what you requested.
gotchas: Users who consented to a narrower set must re-consent to get newly added Gmail scopes (community, f29).

steps.title: Draft the verification package
steps.detail: An agent can draft the scope justification for each Gmail scope, a demo script showing the full flow including the OAuth grant, and the homepage and privacy policy text for your review. Remove any scope the features do not need.
gotchas: Verification submissions for sensitive or restricted scopes must show the complete flow, including the grant step (f10).

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Record a screen capture of the complete app flow from first sign-in through the OAuth grant and the Gmail feature that uses each scope. Publish it at a link Google can open.

steps.title: Submit for verification and keep contacts current
steps.detail: Submit the app for verification from the consent screen. Make sure the project owners and editors have current email addresses, because Google's OAuth review team only communicates by email to those accounts.
gotchas: Changes to an already-approved app can trigger re-verification before users see them (f28).

steps.title: Wait for Google review, then complete the security assessment
steps.detail: Google reviews the submission, then for restricted scopes its Trust and Safety team contacts you to start the annual CASA security assessment by a Google-approved assessor. Community sources put the verification at about six weeks; this was not confirmed by Google.

steps.title: Plan for annual revalidation
steps.detail: Put the yearly revalidation on your calendar. The assurance level can rise if the user base or data handling changes.

scopes.effect: Full mailbox access including IMAP, SMTP and POP3. Triggers verification with demo video and an annual CASA security assessment for public use. This is Composio's default.
Sending mail only. Sensitive, not restricted, per a community reference; verification applies but the CASA assessment should not (community, not confirmed against Google's list).
Listed as non-sensitive in a community reference; not in Composio's defaults. Labels only, so it cannot read message content.
Sign-in scopes. Apps requesting only profile or email sign-in scopes fall under sign-in branding guidelines rather than the full verification path.

scopes.scope: Contacts, birthday, addresses, phone numbers and profile.language.read scopes in Composio's defaults
scopes.effect: Tier not classified in the findings. Check the classification shown in the consent screen before submission, since any sensitive or restricted scope changes the review path.

blockers.symptom: Verification and CASA security assessment required before public users can use Gmail through your client.
blockers.cause: https://mail.google.com/ is a restricted scope, and Composio's default scope list includes it.
blockers.fix: Narrow to the scopes your features need (for example gmail.send or gmail.labels if they fit). If you need the full mailbox, budget for verification and an annual CASA assessment.

blockers.symptom: Test users are asked to re-authorize after about a week, and new users cannot be added past 100.
blockers.cause: External apps in Testing have a 100-user cap and 7-day refresh token expiry (community-reported).
blockers.fix: Use an Internal app if you are in a Workspace organization. Otherwise, plan to re-authorize weekly and keep the test list under 100.

blockers.symptom: Refresh tokens stop working on their own.
blockers.cause: Tokens lapse after six months unused, on revocation, after a password change with Gmail scopes, or at the per-client refresh token limit (community-reported).
blockers.fix: Handle invalid_grant by sending the user back through the consent flow. Do not rely on long-lived refresh tokens for Gmail scopes.

blockers.symptom: Production users cannot grant access until verification passes.
blockers.cause: A community guide says apps past the test-user cap are blocked until verified. Google's own documentation was not checked.
blockers.fix: Treat verification as required before any broad launch. Confirm the rule on Google's official pages before you rely on it.

blockers.symptom: Unknown whether Composio's managed client can be used for external Gmail users.
blockers.cause: Whether Composio's managed Google client is verified for mail.google.com was not established.
blockers.fix: Use your own verified OAuth client for external users. Prototype on managed auth only with your own account.

composio.note: Managed auth is the fast path for prototyping on your own account. Its default scopes include https://mail.google.com/, a restricted scope, so a Composio-brokered Gmail connection still hits restricted-scope review and a CASA assessment for whichever OAuth client owns that scope. For external users, use an OAuth client you control and verify. Whether Composio's managed Google client is verified for these scopes is unknown.
